indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.2.1.3 Demonstrate understanding of how carbon and nitrogen are cycled in nature
indicator.objective: Know the functions of carbon within the environment

skills.description: Identify materials in the environment that contain carbon (e.g. pencils, charcoal, food, carbon dioxide).
State the role of carbon in those materials (e.g. carbon in pencils for writing, carbon in charcoal for fuel).
Recognise carbon dioxide as a gas containing carbon that is used by plants.
Explain simply why carbon is important in the environment.
Demonstrate understanding of carbon’s function through role-play or simple description.
Recognise that carbon is part of food and living things.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Carbon is only found in pencils.
Carbon is not part of living things.
Carbon dioxide is not related to carbon.
Carbon has no function in the environment.

questions.stem: Which of these materials contains carbon?
hints: Pencils are made of graphite and clay.
Graphite is a form of carbon.
questions.explanation: A pencil contains carbon in the form of graphite. Graphite is a form of carbon used for writing.
questions.misconception: Carbon is only found in pencils.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of carbon in the environment?
hints: Charcoal is made from burnt wood.
questions.explanation: Charcoal contains carbon. It is made from wood that has been burned without much air.
questions.misconception: Charcoal does not contain carbon.

questions.stem: Name one material in the environment that contains carbon.
hints: Think about what you write with.
Think about what you burn for fuel.
questions.explanation: Materials that contain carbon include pencils (graphite), charcoal, wood, coal and food.
questions.misconception: Carbon is only found in pencils.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Carbon is only found in pencils.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, carbon is only in pencils
No, carbon is also found in charcoal, food and carbon dioxide
No, carbon is only found in water
No, carbon is only found in stones
questions.explanation: Carbon is found in pencils, but also in charcoal, food, carbon dioxide and many other materials.
questions.misconception: Carbon is only found in pencils.

questions.stem: What is the role of carbon in a pencil?
options: It makes the pencil smell good
hints: The dark part of the pencil is graphite.
questions.explanation: Carbon in the form of graphite helps the pencil write by leaving marks on paper.
questions.misconception: Carbon in pencils is for colour.

questions.stem: What is the role of carbon in charcoal?
options: It helps charcoal burn as fuel
questions.explanation: Carbon in charcoal helps it burn and produce heat for cooking and other uses.
questions.misconception: Charcoal does not use carbon for burning.

questions.stem: State one role of carbon in charcoal.
answer: it makes charcoal a good fuel
it provides heat when charcoal burns
questions.explanation: Carbon in charcoal helps it burn and produce heat.
questions.misconception: Carbon in charcoal is not useful.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Carbon in charcoal is only for colour.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, carbon is only for colour
No, carbon in charcoal is mainly for burning and producing heat
No, carbon in charcoal is for writing
No, carbon in charcoal is for drinking
questions.explanation: Carbon in charcoal is mainly for burning and producing heat, not just for colour.
questions.misconception: Carbon in charcoal is only for colour.

questions.stem: Which gas contains carbon and is used by plants to make food?
hints: Plants take in this gas from the air.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a gas that contains carbon. Plants use it to make food.
questions.misconception: Carbon dioxide is not related to carbon.

questions.stem: What do plants use carbon dioxide for?
hints: Plants need it to make food.
They take it from the air.
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide to make food.
questions.misconception: Plants do not use carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: How is carbon dioxide related to carbon?
options: Carbon dioxide does not contain carbon
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide contains carbon. It is a gas made of carbon and oxygen.
questions.misconception: Carbon dioxide is not related to carbon.

questions.stem: Why is carbon important in the environment?
options: It is part of all living things and helps plants make food
questions.explanation: Carbon is important because it is part of all living things and helps plants make food through carbon dioxide.
questions.misconception: Carbon has no function in the environment.

questions.stem: Give one reason why carbon is important in the environment.
answer: it is part of living things
plants use carbon dioxide to make food
questions.explanation: Carbon is important because it is part of all living things and helps plants make food through carbon dioxide.
questions.misconception: Carbon has no importance.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Carbon is only a pollutant.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, carbon is only a pollutant
No, carbon is also an essential part of living things and helps plants make food
No, carbon is only found in water
hints: Carbon is in all living things.
questions.explanation: Carbon is not only a pollutant; it is an essential part of living things and helps plants make food.
questions.misconception: Carbon is only a pollutant.

questions.stem: In a role-play about carbon, what would a learner acting as carbon in a pencil say?
questions.explanation: A learner acting as carbon in a pencil would say 'I help you write' because carbon in graphite helps pencils write.
questions.misconception: Carbon in pencils is for breathing.

questions.stem: In a role-play, how would you describe the function of carbon in charcoal?
answer: I help charcoal burn and give heat
I make charcoal a good fuel
I help produce heat when charcoal burns
questions.explanation: Carbon in charcoal helps it burn and produce heat, so a learner could say 'I help charcoal burn and give heat.'
questions.misconception: Carbon in charcoal is not useful.

questions.stem: In groups, role-play the functions of carbon in the environment. One learner acts as carbon in a pencil, another as carbon in charcoal, another as carbon dioxide used by plants. Each learner should say one sentence explaining their role. Present to the class.

criteria.description: Acted as carbon in a pencil and explained its role (writing)
Acted as carbon in charcoal and explained its role (burning/fuel)
Acted as carbon dioxide and explained its role (used by plants to make food)
Spoke clearly and participated in the role-play

hints: Think about the role of carbon in each material.
Say one sentence about what carbon does.
questions.explanation: This is a practical/role-play task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Carbon has no function.

questions.stem: Is carbon part of the food we eat?
options: Yes, carbon is part of food
No, food does not contain carbon
questions.explanation: Yes, carbon is part of food because food comes from living things, and all living things contain carbon.
questions.misconception: Food does not contain carbon.

questions.stem: Why is carbon found in food?
answer: because food comes from living things and living things contain carbon
food is made from living things which contain carbon
all living things contain carbon, so food does too
hints: Food comes from plants and animals.
questions.explanation: Carbon is found in food because food comes from living things, and all living things contain carbon.
questions.misconception: Food does not contain carbon.

questions.stem: A learner says, 'Carbon is only found in non-living things like pencils and charcoal.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, carbon is only in non-living things
No, carbon is also found in living things and food
No, carbon is only found in water
No, carbon is only found in air
questions.explanation: Carbon is found in non-living things like pencils and charcoal, but it is also found in living things and food.
questions.misconception: Carbon is not part of living things.
